facts.content: Assessment includes acute upper respiratory tract infection or acute bronchitic illness, most likely viral.

facts.content: Patient to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature at home.

facts.content: Patient to continue symptomatic treatment with Lemsip and avoid other paracetamol-containing products.
facts.source_text: - Continue symptomatic measures (Lemsip as patient is taking). Counseling: Lemsip contains paracetamol (acetaminophen); avoid concurrent paracetamol-containing products.

facts.content: Advise against routine daytime cough syrup; small amount allowed at night if cough prevents sleep.
facts.source_text: - Cough syrup: advise against daytime use routinely; may use small amount at night only if cough prevents sleep.

facts.content: Consider antibiotic therapy if symptoms do not settle or fever persists or worsens, given patient’s diabetes risk.
facts.source_text: - If not settling or if fever persists/worsens, consider antibiotic therapy (per clinician decision) given patient’s diabetes and greater risk for bacterial infection.

facts.content: Patient instructions include obtaining a thermometer, monitoring temperature, maintaining fluids and rest, avoiding extra paracetamol, and using cough suppressant only at night.
facts.source_text: - Patient instructions: obtain a thermometer, monitor temperature, continue fluids and rest, avoid additional paracetamol if taking Lemsip, use cough suppressant only at night if needed for sleep.

facts.content: Ensure regular diabetes follow-up and blood glucose or BMI monitoring with primary care.

facts.content: Ensure routine blood pressure checks with general practitioner.

facts.content: Patient should reassess via telemedicine or in person if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

facts.content: Seek urgent reassessment for persistent fever above 37.5–38°C, worsening cough, new sputum production, hemoptysis, new shortness of breath, chest pain, or other concerning change.
facts.source_text: - Seek urgent reassessment if any of the following develop: persistent fever >37.5–38.0°C (especially if ongoing/spiking), worsening cough, new or increased sputum production, hemoptysis, new shortness of breath, chest pain, or any other concerning change.

facts.content: Return or phone consult if symptoms worsen or do not improve within 7–14 days or sooner for red flags.
